Create a figure with a grid of subplots

Source: R/subplots.R
make_subplots.Rd

Lays out a rows x cols grid of subplots, ported from plotly.py's make_subplots(). Traces and layout objects can then be placed in a cell with the row and col arguments of add_trace(), the add_<trace>() functions, update_xaxes(), add_annotation() and similar functions.

Usage

make_subplots(
  rows = 1,
  cols = 1,
  shared_xaxes = FALSE,
  shared_yaxes = FALSE,
  start_cell = "top-left",
  print_grid = FALSE,
  horizontal_spacing = NULL,
  vertical_spacing = NULL,
  subplot_titles = NULL,
  column_widths = NULL,
  row_heights = NULL,
  specs = NULL,
  insets = NULL,
  column_titles = NULL,
  row_titles = NULL,
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  figure = NULL,
  font = NULL
)

Arguments

rows, cols

Number of rows and columns in the grid.

shared_xaxes, shared_yaxes

Link axes so they pan and zoom together: TRUE (x axes within each column, y axes within each row), "columns", "rows", "all" or FALSE. Tick labels are hidden on all but the outer axes.

start_cell

Which cell is row 1, column 1: "top-left" or "bottom-left".

print_grid

If TRUE, print the grid layout (see print_grid()).

horizontal_spacing, vertical_spacing

Space between columns or rows, as a fraction of the figure width or height. Defaults to 0.2 / cols (0.4 / cols with secondary y axes) and 0.3 / rows (0.5 / rows with subplot titles).

subplot_titles

Character vector of titles, one per subplot in row-major order (insets last). Empty strings are skipped.

column_widths, row_heights

Relative column widths and row heights; default equal.

specs

Per-cell subplot specifications: a list of rows lists, each holding cols elements. Each element is NULL (empty cell) or a named list with any of:

  • type: "xy" (default, 2D cartesian), "scene", "polar", "ternary", "geo", "map", "domain" (e.g. pie charts), or a trace type such as "bar" or "pie" to use its subplot type.

  • secondary_y: TRUE to add a second y axis on the right ("xy" only).

  • colspan, rowspan: number of columns or rows the subplot spans.

  • l, r, b, t: padding on each side, as a fraction of the figure.

insets

List of inset subplots, each a named list with cell (c(row, col) of the cell it sits in), type, and l, b (offsets) and w, h (size, or "to_end") as fractions of the cell.

column_titles, row_titles

Titles above each column and to the right of each row.

x_title, y_title

Titles below and to the left of the whole grid.

figure

An existing go_figure() to add the subplots to.

font

Font for the subplot, column, row and x/y titles: a named list or go_layout_annotation_font() object. Default list(size = 16).

Value

A go_figure with the subplot grid in its layout.

See also

print_grid(), get_subplot()

Examples

fig <- make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2, subplot_titles = c("Left", "Right")) |>
  add_scatter(x = 1:3, y = c(4, 5, 6), row = 1, col = 1) |>
  add_scatter(x = 20:22, y = c(50, 60, 70), row = 1, col = 2) |>
  update_yaxes(title_text = "y", row = 1, col = 1)

# Mixed subplot types and a secondary y axis
fig <- make_subplots(
  rows = 2, cols = 2,
  specs = list(
    list(list(secondary_y = TRUE), list(type = "domain")),
    list(list(colspan = 2), NULL)
  ),
  print_grid = TRUE
)
#> This is the format of your plot grid:
#> [ (1,1) x,y,y2 ]  [ (1,2)        ]
#> [ (2,1) x2,y3            -       ]
